result.topic_en: The page evaluates the imaginary part of a formula (65) at rational points x = 2πm/n, and then proves an Abel-type theorem: if the series a_0 + a_1 + a_2 + ... converges, the power series f(r) tends to its sum as r approaches 1.
result.transcription:
5.
Posito $x=\frac{m}{n}2\pi$ fit pars imaginaria
formulae 65
$1^o$ si $n$ est numerus par
$=\sum_{0,\infty}^{s} -4\pi i \sum_{1,n-1}^{p} (-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}} \frac{1}{p+ns}\left(\frac{pm}{n}+\frac{1}{2}\right)(-1)^{\frac{n}{2}s}$
$2^o$ si $n$ est numerus impar
$=\sum_{0,\infty}^{s} -4\pi i \sum_{1,2n-1}^{p} (-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}} \frac{1}{p+2ns}\left(\frac{pm}{n}+\frac{1}{2}\right)(-1)^{s}$
quam patet habere valorem finitum,
nisi $n$ est $\equiv 0 \bmod 4$.

Convergentia summae
$a_0+a_1+a_2+a_3\ldots$
postulat, ut data quantitate quamvis
parva $\varepsilon$ assignari possit terminus $a_n$,
a quo summa usque ad terminum
quemvis $a_m$ extensa nanciscatur
valorem absolutum ipso $\varepsilon$ mino-
rem. Iam posito brevitatis gratia
$\varepsilon_{n+1}=a_{n+1}$
$\varepsilon_{n+2}=a_{n+1}+a_{n+2}$
$\varepsilon_{n+3}=a_{n+1}+a_{n+2}+a_{n+3}$
$\ldots\ldots\ldots$
functio
$f(r)=a_0+a_1r+a_2r^2+\ldots+\ldots$
facile sub hac forma exhibetur
$=a_0+a_1r+a_2r^2\ldots a_nr^n+\varepsilon_{n+1}r^{n+1}+(\varepsilon_{n+2}-\varepsilon_{n+1})r^{n+2}+(\varepsilon_{n+3}-\varepsilon_{n+2})r^{n+3}$
$=a_0\ldots\ldots a_nr^n+\varepsilon_{n+1}(r^{n+1}-r^{n+2})+\varepsilon_{n+2}(r^{n+2}-r^{n+3})+\ldots$
Unde patet convergente $r$ versus limitem
1 functionem $f(r)$ tandem quavis quan-
titate minus a valore seriei
$a_0+a_1+a_2\ldots$
distare. Summa terminorum al-
tioris gradus quam $n$, quum sint
$\varepsilon_{n+1}, \varepsilon_{n+2}\ldots$ ex hyp. omnes omisso
[-(abjecto)-] signo $<\varepsilon$, differentiaeque
$r^{n+1}-r^{n+2}\ldots$ omnes positivae,
manifesto evadit quantitate absoluta
